label: Yakutian horse

names.text: Alternate names as given in the research input. The fetched article text did not list them, so the page does not confirm them; 'Yakutian horse' is the article title.

about.text: A horse of Yakutia (the Sakha Republic) in Siberia, Russia, that survives extreme cold without shelter. Its milk is mostly made into kumis.

sources.text: Article text: milk used 'mostly for making kumis'; kept in Yakutia (Sakha Republic), Siberia; survives temperatures down to −70 °C without shelter.

Horses likely descend from stock brought by the Yakuts when they migrated to the area beginning in the 13th century; the article says they have been in Siberia for roughly 800 years and that a 2015 study places their introduction a few centuries ago. No formation year range is given, so none is recorded.
Article text: milk used mostly for making kumis. The article names no other use.
Article text: 'FAO (2007): not at risk', with a figure of 99 it does not explain. Taken as the article reports it; not checked against DAD-IS itself.

facts.v: Survives without shelter at temperatures reaching −70 °C, and uncovers grass under up to 50 cm of snow.

sources.text: Article text: survives without shelter at temperatures reaching −70 °C (−94 °F); can uncover grass under up to 50 cm of snow. No year given.

gaps: No milk yield, lactation length, population figure or year was found in the article. The research input's claim of 'at least nine' kumis varieties is not in the article and is not used. The 2015 study the article cites on introduction was not opened. Milk composition was not found.
